newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom deal on job cuts worries Belgian gov't.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom deal on job cuts worries Belgian gov't.

text.p: Belgacom SA, Belgium's partially privatised state telephone company, on Friday said it had reached a landmark deal with unions on job cuts, but the government warned it would scrutinise the agreement closely.

In a statement, Belgacom said it would offer up to 6,500 of its 26,000 workers early retirement from the age of 50, guaranteeing them 75 percent of their last monthly salary until the age of 60 -- the age at which workers are legally allowed to claim early retirement.

However, Pensions Minister Marcel Colla told a news conference after the government's weekly cabinet meeting that the early retirement plan could set a dangerous precedent and cost the social security system dearly.
"I don't want to create any dangerous precedents in the delicate area of pensions," he said.

Colla declined to say if the government might use its 51 percent controlling interest in Belgacom to block the move. Belgacom's other shareholders include Ameritech, Singapore Telecom and TeleDanmark.
"For the moment I have not blocked it. I have done nothing for the simple reason I have not received any official notification of the agreement....I want to react wisely," Colla said.

The government announced separately on Friday it had approved the transfer of about 496 Belgacom staff working in the areas of television licences and maritime radio to the publicly run telecommunications industry regulator.
